releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.13.0
releasesInRange.body:
This release adds the `pnpm profile` and `pnpm token` commands, the `storeIndexFormat: files` setting for stores shared over a network filesystem, and faster Python dependency resolution.

### Minor Changes

- Added the `pnpm profile` command to view and update registry user profile settings.

- Added `pnpm token` to list, create, and revoke authentication tokens on the registry.

- Added the `storeIndexFormat` setting. Set it to `files` to keep a store's package index as one file per package instead of the SQLite `index.db`, for a store on a network filesystem that several machines use at once. SQLite's locking does not work across machines, so concurrent installs on such a store could corrupt `index.db`.

- Added the `nodePackageMap` setting, which groups the package-map settings. `nodePackageMap.mode: write-only` writes `node_modules/.package-map.json` for other tools without making Node.js load it. `mode: load` also makes Node.js load the map, like `nodeExperimentalPackageMap: true`. `nodePackageMap.type` replaces `nodePackageMapType`. The old settings still work [#14937](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14937).

  ```yaml
  nodePackageMap:
    mode: write-only
    type: loose
  ```

### Patch Changes

#### Setting up pnpm

- `pnpm setup` now works when pnpm was installed with npm on macOS. It installed pnpm from npm's `bin` directory and left a `$PNPM_HOME/bin/pnpm` that could not run [#16855](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16855).

- pnpm runs again after `pnpm setup` when `globalShims` enables pnpm. Every command failed with "the global target of the pnpm shim points back at the shim" [#16874](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16874).

- A pnpm built for the MinGW target on Windows, such as the MSYS2 package, now installs the MinGW Rust toolchain that `rust-toolchain.toml` names. It used to install the MSVC toolchain.

#### Installing packages

- On macOS, `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_WRITE_FILE` when the project is on a virtiofs or SMB share. pnpm now falls back to a regular `fsync` when the file system rejects a full sync [#16846](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16846).

- On macOS, `pnpm install`, `pnpm patch-commit`, and other commands that load a pnpmfile no longer hang at random.

- `pnpm install` now puts the executables of a Python build backend's requirements on the `PATH` while the backend runs. Projects built with `uv_build` now install. Before, they failed with "uv-build was not properly installed".

- Removing a `link:` dependency now also removes its symlink from `node_modules` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#16884](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16884).

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` no longer records the tarball URL of a package installed from a scoped registry, such as one set by `@types:registry=`, when pnpm can rebuild the URL from that registry [#16866](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16866).

#### Packing, auditing, and pipelines

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now pack only `pa

prs.title: feat(cli): implement token command
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements `pnpm token` in pnpm v12, replacing the "not implemented" stub. It follows npm 11's `token` command:

- `pnpm token list` (`ls`, default) fetches every page of `GET /-/npm/v1/tokens`, following `urls.next` on the registry's origin. Human-readable, `--json`, and `--parseable` output.
- `pnpm token revoke <id|token...>` (`rm`, `delete`, `remove`) resolves each argument by key prefix or token value, then sends `DELETE /-/npm/v1/tokens/token/<key>`.
- `pnpm token create [--read-only] [--cidr <cidr>]` asks for the account password and posts it with `readonly` and `cidr_whitelist`.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Implement `pnpm token` (list, revoke, create) against the npm token API,
following npm 11's command.

- list follows `urls.next` while it stays on the registry origin, with a
  bound on the number of pages.
- revoke accepts several ids or token values. A key-prefix match revokes
  by key; a token value is sent as-is, as npm does. The path segment is
  percent-encoded. Diagnostics show at most the first 8 characters of an
  argument, since it may be a live token. Repeated arguments are revoked
  once, and a failure partway reports how many were already revoked.
- create sends its POST once, since a retry after a lost response would
  mint another live token. It prompts for the password (masked on a terminal, first stdin
  line otherwise) because the registry requires it.
- Requests use a client whose redirects are limited to the registry
  origin.
```

prs.title: feat(cli): implement profile command
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements `pnpm profile` in pnpm v12. It replaces the "not implemented, use npm" stub and follows npm's `profile` command and the registry's `-/npm/v1/user` protocol:

- `get [<key>...]`: shows the profile as a table, the values of the given keys, `--json`, or `--parseable`. A pending 2FA setup shows as `disabled`.
- `set <key> <value>`: sends the change together with the other writable fields, because the registry clears the ones left out. `set password` prompts for the current and new password and rejects a value on the command line.
- `enable-2fa [auth-only|auth-and-writes]`: prompts for the password and resets a pending setup. On first setup it shows a QR code and the secret, sends the authenticator code, and prints the recovery codes. It rejects `--json` and `--parseable`.
- `disable-2fa`: prompts for the password. If 2FA is not enabled, it says so.

Every argument is validated before credentials are resolved. Registry replies are read through the size limit. An unreadable or malformed reply is an error. A 401 OTP challenge asks for `--otp`.

Not covered, unlike npm: interactive OTP prompting on an EOTP challenge (pass `--otp`), and converting legacy basic auth to a bearer token before enabling 2FA.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Implement `pnpm profile` (get, set, enable-2fa, disable-2fa) against the
registry's -/npm/v1/user endpoint, following npm's profile command.

prs.title: feat(package-map): group package-map settings under nodePackageMap
prs.author: EnginKARATAS
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#14937.

Adds a `nodePackageMap` setting to pnpm v12 that groups the package-map settings:

```yaml
nodePackageMap:
  mode: write-only   # off (default) | write-only | load
  type: loose        # standard (default) | loose
```

- `write-only` writes `node_modules/.package-map.json` during isolated and hoisted installs, but scripts do not get Node's `--experimental-package-map` option. Other tools can read the dependency graph and script resolution does not change.
- `load` behaves like `nodeExperimentalPackageMap: true`. pnpm writes the map and Node loads it in pnpm-managed scripts.
- `nodePackageMap.type` replaces `nodePackageMapType`.

`nodeExperimentalPackageMap` and `nodePackageMapType` shipped in v11.8.0 and keep working as deprecated spellings. When one source sets both spellings, `nodePackageMap` wins. The environment variables are `PNPM_CONFIG_NODE_PACKAGE_MAP_MODE` and `PNPM_CONFIG_NODE_PACKAGE_MAP_TYPE`.

This PR also changes how the map file is written. On its first creation it now goes through a temp file and `rename`, so tools reading `.package-map.json` never see a partial file.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Add a nodePackageMap section that groups the package-map settings, so
tools can consume pnpm's dependency graph without changing how Node
resolves modules during scripts.

nodePackageMap.mode is off, write-only, or load. write-only writes
node_modules/.package-map.json for isolated and hoisted installs without
adding --experimen

prs.title: fix(rust-toolchain): install the MinGW toolchain from a MinGW-built pnpm
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
Refs #16854

## Problem

During `pnpm install`, pnpm installs the Rust toolchain that `rust-toolchain.toml` names. On Windows the host triple was hard-coded to `*-pc-windows-msvc`. A pnpm built for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, such as the MSYS2 package, therefore downloaded and linked an MSVC toolchain (`Installing Rust 1.97.0 (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)`), which a MinGW build cannot use.

## Fix

On Windows, the ABI of the toolchain to install now follows the target pnpm itself was built for. rustup takes its default host from its own build in the same way.

| pnpm built for | toolchain installed |
| --- | --- |
| `*-pc-windows-gnu` | `*-pc-windows-gnu` |
| `*-pc-windows-gnullvm` | `*-pc-windows-gnullvm` |
| anything else | `*-pc-windows-msvc` (unchanged) |

If the distribution server publishes no toolchain for that host, pnpm keeps its existing behaviour: it warns and leaves the toolchain to rustup.

## Workaround until this ships

Packagers who don't want pnpm to download a toolchain can run `pnpm install --config.runtime-on-fail=ignore`. Any `runtimeOnFail` value other than `download` skips toolchain installation.

## Testing

`cargo clippy` and `cargo nextest run -p pnpm-rust-toolchain` pass on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. The GNU branches were not compiled locally because those targets aren't installed here.

prs.title: fix(pipeline): select the root in a root-only workspace
prs.author: TrevorBurnham
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm pipeline` left out the workspace root unless `includeWorkspaceRoot` was set. In a workspace whose `packages` list only the root, or omit `packages`, it ran nothing. Recursive commands keep the root in that case, so the pipeline now uses the same root-only guard (`is_root_only_patterns`). An empty full-mode selection also no longer reports "No projects are affected since <base>".

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16849

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`pnpm pipeline` dropped the workspace root unless `includeWorkspaceRoot`
was set, so a workspace whose `packages` list only the root (or omit
`packages`) had nothing to run. Recursive commands keep the root in that
case; the pipeline and `AutoExcludeRoot::root_selector` now share one
rule, `keeps_workspace_root`, decided once in `run_pipeline` and carried on
`SelectAffectedOptions`.

In a root-only workspace every changed file maps to the root, which sent
each affected run down the workspace-root-files branch with a warning and
a full run. That branch now applies only when the run covers more than
the root.

The guard is pattern-based, as in recursive commands: `packages:
['packages/*']` with no matching directories still excludes the root.

An empty selection in full mode no longer reports "No projects are
affected since <base>".

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16849
```

prs.title: fix(python-installer): drop empty PATH entries for backend hooks
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#16865, covering review findings that landed after it merged.

An empty `PATH` entry names the current directory, which for a Python backend hook is the project. The hook `PATH` had one when `PATH` was unset (`split_paths("")` yields one empty entry), and kept any empty entries in a set `PATH` (`a::b`, a leading or trailing separator). The hook `PATH` now keeps only non-empty inherited entries, as `path_outside` already does for interpreter discovery.

The `PATH` construction moves into `hook_path`, which unit tests cover. The empty-entry test fails when the filter is removed.

No changeset, because the bug exists only in unreleased code from pnpm/pnpm#16865.

backend hook is the project. The hook PATH had one when PATH was unset
(`split_paths("")` yields one empty entry), and kept any empty entries
in a set PATH. A backend looking up a command its build environment
does not install could then run a file the project ships.

The hook PATH now keeps only non-empty inherited entries, as

prs.title: feat(store-dir): add a per-package-file store index for shared stores
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds the `storeIndexFormat` setting. With `storeIndexFormat: files`, the store keeps its package index as one file per package under `<store>/package-index/` instead of the SQLite `index.db`.

This is for a store on a filesystem that several machines mount at once, such as a CI cache shared by many jobs. SQLite's WAL mode coordinates processes through a shared-memory file and file locks that only work within one machine. On such a share every index lookup and write is a network round trip, and concurrent installs corrupt `index.db`.

I reproduced this with containers that mount an sshfs share with 1 ms latency and install a project with about 1,300 packages:

| | `sqlite` | `files` |
|---|---|---|
| one job, cold store | 47 s | 41 s |
| one job, warm store | 21 s | 22 s |
| two concurrent cold jobs | both pass, `index.db` left corrupt (`btreeInitPage() returns error code 11`) | both pass, 1,299 intact entries, no leftover temp files |

In a fuller run (Bit + fusepm signing a component, two jobs at once), the corruption also failed the jobs with `database disk image is malformed`.

sshfs does not pass POSIX locks between clients, so it is the worst case for SQLite. NFSv4 does pass locks, but WAL's shared memory is still per host.

cache shared by many jobs, cannot hold index.db. SQLite's WAL mode
coordinates processes through a shared-memory file and file locks that

prs.title: fix(audit): skip runtime entries when auditing
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16869.

`pnpm audit signatures` reported a `devEngines.runtime` entry (`node@runtime:24.21.0`) as having an invalid registry signature ("Missing lockfile integrity for node@24.21.0").

The audit request's `package_version` dropped the `runtime:` prefix, so the runtime entered the request as the npm package `node@24.21.0`. Since 12.10.0, `audit signatures` binds verification to the lockfile integrity. It looked up `node@24.21.0` in the lockfile, found nothing, and flagged the package. Before 12.10.0 it "verified" against the unrelated npm `node` package's integrity.

`package_version` now returns `None` for `runtime:` entries, so `audit` and `audit signatures` both leave runtimes out. This matches pnpm v11. I checked that `pnpm@11 audit signatures` on the issue's repro reports `audited 1 package` and exits 0, so v11 is unaffected and needs no change.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`package_version` dropped the `runtime:` prefix, so a `devEngines.runtime`
entry such as `node@runtime:24.21.0` entered the audit request as the npm
package `node@24.21.0`. `audit signatures` then looked up `node@24.21.0` in
the lockfile, found no integrity, and since 12.10.0 reported it as an
invalid signature. The vulnerability audit likewise queried advisories for
the unrelated npm `node` package.

Runtime entries are now excluded from the audit request, matching pnpm v11,
which already leaves them out.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16869
```

prs.title: fix(hooks): keep the pnpmfile worker from holding pnpm's pipes on macOS
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the intermittent macOS CI timeout of `hooks::update_config_applies_to_patch_commit_and_patch_remove` (seen on run 38243837603 for pnpm/pnpm#16865 and on run 38085392828). The cause is a product deadlock, not a test problem.

**Root cause.** macOS has no `pipe2`, so the standard library creates a child's pipes with `pipe()` and only then marks them close-on-exec. A child spawned on another thread between those two steps inherits the pipe. The `pnpm patch-commit` reresolving install spawns the pnpmfile worker (`node --input-type commonjs -e ...`) on one thread while `detect_installability_host` runs `node --version` through `Command::output()` on a blocking thread. When the worker inherited the write end of the probe's stdout pipe:

- pnpm sat in `detect_node_version` → `Command::output` → `read_to_end` waiting for EOF,
- the worker held the write end and stays alive until pnpm closes its stdin, which happens only when pnpm exits.

Neither side has a timeout, so the test waited until nextest killed it at 300s.

**Evidence.** I reproduced the hang deterministically with a DYLD interposer that sleeps a random 0 to 100 ms after `pipe()`, which widens the race window. When the test hung, `lsof` showed the worker holding both ends (fd 18/19) of a pipe that pnpm was still reading on fd 18. The `node --version` child had already exited and was a zombie. `sample` showed pnpm blocked in `pnpm_graph_hasher::engine_name::detect_node_version` → `std::process::Command::out
…(truncated)

prs.title: perf(python): read index metadata files and fetch ahead while resolving
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Addresses the Python install slowness reported in https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/3164#discussioncomment-18875448.

Python resolution was serial. The solver named one missing index page or one version's metadata, pnpm fetched it, and the solver ran again. Each version's metadata came out of the whole wheel, which pnpm downloaded and handed to the interpreter. Wheel downloads after resolution were already concurrent. Resolution was not.

This PR changes two things:

1. **PEP 658 metadata files.** Resolution reads the metadata file an index publishes beside a wheel.
   - The file is checked against the SHA-256 on the index page. A file advertised without a SHA-256 is not read, and the wheel is read instead.
   - It is cached under `python-metadata-v1`, so offline resolutions can reuse it.
   - Indexes that publish no such file, and offline runs without a cached copy, still read the wheel.
   - Wheels are downloaded only for selected releases, through the existing concurrent `fetch_wheels`. Build environments, which install straight from a resolution, now go through `fetch_selected_wheels`.
2. **Read ahead (`resolver/ahead.rs`).** Read ahead is the speculative fetching of index pages and metadata files before the solver asks for them.
   - Pages are read for everything a requirement or a read metadata file names.
   - Metadata is read for the version the solver will likely pick: the highest version the requirements admit, preferring a final release.
   - Rea

prs.title: fix(shim): run a global target that is a hard link of the shim
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16874.

With `globalShims` enabling pnpm, `pnpm setup` hard-links the running executable as the `pnpm` shim, and the store imports the global `pnpm` package's bin from that same file, also by hard link. The native shim's self-recursion guard compared file identity, so it took the global target for the shim itself and every command failed with "the global target of the pnpm shim points back at the shim".

The guard now compares canonical paths, with file identity kept as a cheap first filter. A hard link elsewhere runs under its own path, finds no sidecar there, and runs the CLI, so it cannot recurse. A target that names the shim, directly or through a symlink, still fails.

Reproduced with the released 12.11.2 binary in a get.pnpm.io-style layout (executable + `dist/` in a temp dir, `globalShims: { pnpm: auto }`): the shim, the global package bin, and the temp executable all share one inode. With this change, `pnpm -v` works, including after the temp dir is removed.

v11 has no native shims, so this is v12-only.

prs.title: fix(python): keep a read-ahead page error from hiding a distribution
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#16881 with the review findings that landed after it merged. Both bugs exist only in unreleased code, so this PR has no new changeset. It edits the pending one instead.

- **A read-ahead page error no longer hides a distribution.** `record_index` inserted an empty candidate list before parsing the page. When a page read ahead failed to parse, the error was set aside, because nothing had asked for that page yet. The empty list stayed behind, so the solver saw a distribution with no versions and never asked for the page again. `main` would fail with a misleading no-versions error instead of the page's own error. The list is now inserted only after the page parses.
- **Mixed metadata markers.** An index can declare the metadata file in both fields: `core-metadata: true`, plus `dist-info-metadata` with a SHA-256. pnpm now takes the field that publishes the SHA-256, so it reads the file instead of downloading the wheel.
- **Changeset wording.** The changeset states the measured speedup instead of "much faster", with one change per sentence, and gives the old timing its own sentence.

Tests:
- `an_unreadable_page_read_ahead_fails_with_its_own_error`: one root dependency's page is slow and the other's is unparsable, tried in both orders.
- `candidates_carry_the_metadata_file_an_index_advertises` gains the mixed-field case.

Both tests fail without their fix. All 341 Python tests, clippy, and dylint pass locally.

prs.title: perf(deps-resolver): leave lockfile-reused subtrees out of the warm-up
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A fresh resolution against an existing lockfile reuses most of that lockfile's subtrees, and the walk never consults registry metadata for a reused subtree. The speculative warm-up that prefetches packuments during the walk did not know that: it resolved the **whole** subtree of every freshly seeded node through the resolver, with no lockfile key, so every child went to metadata. On a repeat install of a 5,100-package workspace that was about 5,650 metadata lookups the install never needed — 22 s of a 28 s resolution against a store and metadata cache on a network filesystem.

The warm-up now derives each child's lockfile key the way the walk does (from the snapshot the parent landed on) and skips a child whose subtree the walk will reuse. A child the lockfile cannot reproduce is still warmed, and so are its children. Whether a child is reused is decided per importer, so a package counts as warmed only when none of its children was skipped; otherwise the next importer that reaches it warms the children it cannot reuse.

Measured on that workspace, with the store on an sshfs share (1 ms latency), warm store, Bit's `enableModulesDir: false` install:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| metadata lookups during resolution | 5,657 | 2,483 |
| `resolve_workspace` | 28.5 s | 14.2 s |

prs.title: perf(package-manager): verify the store while a store-only install resolves
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A run that fetches into the store without writing `node_modules` (`enableModulesDir: false`, what Bit's fusepm uses) resolves against a lockfile, prefetches what it resolves, and then fetches the packages it reused from the lockfile. Those reused packages are most of a repeat install, and their store verification — reading every row, then one `stat` per file — ran only after the resolution, with nothing to overlap. On a 5,100-package workspace with the store on a network filesystem that was a 19 s gap between `build_fresh_lockfile` and the end of the install, during which nothing else happened.

Two changes:

1. **Verification starts with the resolution.** When the run fetches into the store and has a wanted lockfile, `set_up_resolvers` starts `prefetch_cas_paths` over the lockfile's registry entries as soon as the store index is open, against the verified-files cache the resolution shares (`StoreVerification`). `finish_fresh_fetch` awaits it and hands its rows to `fetch_missing`, which drops them before any row is read again, and the prefetcher inherits the cache so the leftover rows do not stat the same files twice.
2. **A package's files are checked in parallel.** `PendingFilesCheck::verify` stat'ed a row's files one after another, so a 7,000-file package held the verification's tail for 10 s on that filesystem. From 32 files a row's checks run on the rayon pool. Every file is still checked.

prs.title: perf(store-dir): read a per-file index entry outside the shared handle's lock
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The shared read-only store index (`SharedReadonlyStoreIndex`) is a `Mutex<StoreIndex>`, and every lookup through it held the lock while the backend read: the tarball prefetcher's `read_row`, the npm resolver's cached-manifest peek, and the offline store view. That is right for SQLite, whose connection is not `Sync`, but needless for `storeIndexFormat: files` (#16875): its rows are independent files, and on a network filesystem each read is a round trip. Lookups that rayon and tokio fan out were serialized on the mutex, one round trip at a time.

`StoreIndex::get_shared` / `contains_shared` take the lock only long enough to see which backend the index has. A per-file index is cloned out (a path) and read with the lock released; SQLite is still queried under the lock. The three call sites go through them, and a poisoned lock still reads as a miss.

On a 5,100-package store-only install against a per-file index on an sshfs share (1 ms latency), this took the warm install from ~58 s to ~51 s; the SQLite path is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(remove): unlink a removed link: dependency under the hoisted linker
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16884

## Problem

With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, removing a direct `link:` dependency updated `package.json` and the lockfile but left its symlink in `node_modules`, so the package stayed importable. Both v12 (Rust) and v11 (TypeScript) were affected.

The hoisted linker's orphan diff only covers the package directories it imports. The stale direct-dependency prune that the isolated linker runs is skipped for the hoisted layout. So nothing removed the links it writes for `link:` and workspace dependencies.

## Fix

Before the hoisted tree is linked, unlink every direct-dependency symlink that the wanted lockfile no longer records at the same version, removing its bins first. Only symlinks (junctions on Windows) are touched. Real directories stay with the orphan diff.

- **v12:** `prune_stale_hoisted_direct_links` in `prune_stale_modules.rs` reuses `remove_direct_dep_link` and the same containment checks as `PruneStaleModules`. It runs from the hoisted linker next to the existing workspace-hoist cleanup, and both passes now live in `hoisted/stale_links.rs` to keep `hoisted.rs` under the file-length limit. `HoistedLinkerError::PruneWorkspaceHoists` is renamed to `PruneStaleLinks` because it now covers both passes.
- **v11:** `unlinkStaleDirectLinks` runs from `linkHoistedLayout`. `unlinkIfSymlink` moved out of `linkIsolatedLayout.ts` into its own module so both layouts can use it.

Neither implementation removes a `@scope` directory left

prs.title: fix(pack): ship only the always-included files when files is empty
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` packed every file in the package when `files` was an empty array. `build_files_matcher` returned `None` when no entry compiled, so the packlist treated `"files": []` as if the field were missing. npm-packlist and pnpm v11 treat any `files` array as an allowlist, so an empty one ships only `package.json`, the README, the license, and the `main`/`bin` targets.

The matcher is now built for every `files` array, and an empty one matches nothing. A matcher that fails to compile also matches nothing, so no path falls back to packing every file. This is v12-only: v11 uses npm-packlist and already packs only `package.json` for the repro in the issue.

Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16889

## Squash Commit Body

```text
build_files_matcher returned None when no `files` entry compiled, and

prs.title: fix(git-resolver): look up a git ref once per install
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16899.

With `linkWorkspacePackages` enabled, the dependency walk scopes its resolution cache per project (`project_relative_cache_scope`), so a git dependency shared by many workspace projects reaches the git resolver once per project. The git resolver kept nothing between calls, so each project ran its own `git ls-remote`. On an install that re-resolves (a new or changed pnpmfile, `autoDedupe`), that is about one second per project for a remote repo.

`GitResolver` now memoizes its resolutions per specifier. The resolver is built per install (and per call for the NAPI resolve entry point), so a moving branch is still looked up again on the next install. Concurrent requests for one specifier wait on the first through a `tokio::sync::OnceCell`. A failure is not cached, so the next request retries it.

Reproduced locally with a 5-project workspace, a tagged `git+file://` dependency through `catalog:`, and `linkWorkspacePackages: true`: re-resolving made 5 `ls-remote` calls before the change and 1 after.

pnpm v11: not changed. Its git resolver returns the locked resolution (`resolveExistingGitPkg`) before running `ls-remote` whenever the lockfile already has the dependency. I did not run v11 against the repro.

Not in this PR: v12 still runs the one lookup even when the lockfile already records the commit. Its git resolver has no `currentPkg` fast path yet (see the note in `resolving-git-resolver/src/lib.rs`), and a pnpmfile checksum change drops t

prs.title: fix(resolver): decide a dependency that is also an optional peer at its children owner
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`ajv-formats` lists `ajv` both as a dependency and as an optional peer. Since 11.28.0 (pnpm/pnpm#15503) it could end up with `ajv` neither way.

`X` lists `B` as a dependency and as an optional peer. If an ancestor already provides `B`, `X` takes it as a peer. Otherwise it keeps `B` as its own dependency.

What the packages declare:

```
project
├── G
│   └── P
│       ├── B
│       └── X      (dependency: B, also optional peer: B)
└── O              (optional peers: P, B)
```

`X` is reached twice:

```
project
├── G > P > X      ← 1. initial resolution: B is not above X → B is X's dependency
├── O
├── P > X          ← 2. O's optional peers P and B are placed at the project root:
└── B                   B is above X → B is X's peer
```

The shallower occurrence (2) should decide.

- **v11:** `X`'s peer list came from occurrence 1 and its dependencies from occurrence 2, so `B` was in neither. Now both come from occurrence 2. In the issue, `X` = `ajv-formats`, `B` = `ajv`, `P` = `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`.
- **v12:** occurrence 2 reused `X`'s dependencies from occurrence 1. That works, but the lockfile differed from v11's. Occurrence 2 now resolves them again when `B`'s position differs.

Both versions now write the same lockfile as 11.27.1 for the issue's repro: `ajv-formats@3.0.1(ajv@8.20.0)`.

prs.title: fix: stop a stalled update check from holding an up-to-date install, and trace the fast path
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Related to pnpm/pnpm#16839 (a `pnpm install` that prints "Already up to date" after minutes on Windows, with nothing in the `TRACE` output).

Two changes:

1. **The update check no longer holds the command.** `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` start the daily update check alongside the command and awaited it before printing `Done in ...`. With a registry that accepts the connection but never answers (a firewall that drops packets, a proxy that stalls), that wait is the registry client's connect and read timeouts, a minute each, on an install that had nothing else to do. The command no longer waits for it at all: a check the registry has answered has already printed its notice and recorded itself, and one still running when the command is done is aborted and records nothing, so the next command asks again. That is what pnpm v11 does (`checkForUpdates(config).catch(() => {})` in `main.ts`), so the stall is v12-only.

   This only reaches an install that did not take the pre-runtime fast path (a pnpmfile, a frozen lockfile, `workspaces` in `package.json`, per-project lockfiles, config dependencies), because that fast path returns before the runtime exists. The reporter's install prints "Already up to date" with no `repeat-install fast path skipped` line, which is exactly the shape of an install that went through the engine, found nothing to do, and then waited on something silent.
